Classic Hanukkah Potato Latkes

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Makes about 12-15 latkes (Serves 4-6)Prep 25 minCook 30 min

Potato Latkes are crispy, savory pancakes traditionally enjoyed during the Jewish holiday of Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights. Their preparation involves frying in oil, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that burned for eight days in the Temple. Served hot, they are a beloved centerpiece of Hanukkah celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900g) Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled
  • 1 medium (150g) yellow onion, peeled
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 1/4 cup (30g) all-purpose flour or matzo meal
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 3-4 cups (700-950ml) vegetable oil, canola oil, or grapeseed oil, for frying
  • Applesauce and sour cream, for serving (optional)

Method

  1. Grate the potatoes using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor. Immediately transfer the grated potatoes to a large bowl of cold water to prevent browning.
  2. Grate the onion using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor.
  3. Drain the grated potatoes thoroughly. Place them in a clean kitchen towel or several layers of cheesecloth and wring out as much liquid as possible. This step is crucial for crispy latkes.
  4. In a large bowl, combine the well-drained grated potatoes, grated onion, beaten eggs, flour (or matzo meal), salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined.
  5. Heat about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) of oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron works well) over medium-high heat until shimmering, about 350°F (175°C).
  6. Carefully drop spoonfuls (about 2 tablespoons each) of the potato mixture into the hot oil, flattening them slightly with the back of the spoon to form thin pancakes. Do not overcrowd the skillet.
  7. Fry for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
  8. Remove the latkes from the skillet with a slotted spoon or spatula and place them on a wire rack set over a baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
  9. Serve immediately with applesauce and sour cream, if desired.

Tips

  • For extra crispy latkes, ensure you squeeze out as much liquid as possible from the grated potatoes and onions.
  • Keep fried latkes warm in a single layer on a baking sheet in a 200°F (95°C) oven while you finish frying the rest.
  • For a slightly different flavor, add a pinch of garlic powder or a tablespoon of chopped fresh chives to the potato mixture.
